messages:
Alex P.: Quick follow-up to RFC — ran into a gap when rotating KMS keys for Private tenants. Observed some requests routing to Hosted fallback fail because sidecar couldn't decrypt creds.
Mia T.: Brief log snippet?
Alex P.: ```2024-03-12T10:23:45Z ERROR decrypt: kms: access denied key=projects/rdw/keyrings/prod/keys/tenant-42```
Devin L.: hmm ok. Is this the case where sidecar fetches key metadata from control plane and caches ARN? If control plane rotates keys, sidecar still uses cached ARN and fails until restart.
Alex P.: Exactly. TTL is 1h now. In our test the rotation happened immediately after TTL but before sidecar could refresh in time — ~2m outage for a handful of tenants.
Ryan C.: Why did routing fallback to Hosted? Shouldn't requests stay local to Private until key handshake succeeded?
Ashley K.: We have a policy: route by authz then capacity. If sidecar returns error it's treated as permanent and request falls back. That made sense for secret-missing, but not for transient key rotation.
Mia T.: Re the semantics — we need to distinguish >=403 vs transient-decrypt-errors. Maybe add error classes and introduce a grace period.
Alex P.: Proposed short-term: classify decrypt failures with a `retryable` tag when KMS returns specific codes; don't failover for X seconds (linear backoff + retry).
Devin L.: Short-term makes sense. Long-term: consider moving key metadata to local runtime store with streaming updates from control plane (push) instead of TTL pull.
Ryan C.: Streaming updates look nice but brings more coupling and auth surface for Private. Need secure mTLS channel or signed tokens. Also impacts control-plane scale.
Ashley K.: Tradeoff list: push -> lower latency, higher coupling; pull w/short TTL -> eventual consistency; push w/verify-signed-msg -> middle ground.
InfraBot: NOTE: audit schema v2 -> v3 required if we add push; rotation events must be logged per-tenant (ticket: #INF-924).
Mia T.: Can we do hybrid? push for rotation events only (control-plane emits rotation event), sidecar keeps mirror, and fallback policy uses error class + short suppress window.
Devin L.: That feels good. Implementation plan: (1) add error-classification mapping in runtime, (2) control-plane emits rotation webhook to tenant-sidecar (signed JWT), (3) sidecar updates key metadata and triggers warm re-decrypt, (4) fallback window = 60s default.
Alex P.: + add config flag for Private to opt-in since some customers want no control-plane pushes.
Ryan C.: Also we must update admission docs — key re-fetch could spike control-plane on mass rotation; throttle webhooks and batch.
Ashley K.: I'll draft an RFC with sequence diagrams + security checklist. @Devin L. can you prototype error mapping and suppression in runtime?
Devin L.: Yep, will prototype next week. I'll post a short follow-up thread with perf numbers.
Ashley K.: +1 thanks. :thumbsup:
